scope: README.md, AGENTS.md, workers/AGENTS.md, docs/** (alias sources only)

nodes.label: Web UI
nodes.role: App Router pages (app, auth, landing, maintenance), shared components, client hooks and navigation. Server components read through plan/billing services; client code calls /api/v1 routes.

tests.via: e2e (drives pages by URL, no import)

constraints.rule: Read DESIGN.md and the named chapters of docs/styles/design-system.md before changing UI, shared components or tokens.

source.subject: feat(ui): adopt the midnight palette and refine pre-launch screens (#905)

nodes.label: API routes
nodes.role: Next.js route handlers: /api/v1 product API, Clerk webhook, /api/internal/maintenance operator routes, health and OpenAPI docs.

constraints.rule: Internal /api/internal routes bypass Clerk middleware and authenticate with shared maintenance tokens.

source.subject: test(api): expect explicit regenerate orchestration deps

nodes.label: Request boundary
nodes.role: Everything a request passes before product code: proxy (CSP, site gate, Clerk middleware), auth wrappers, per-request RLS client, rate limits, error contract, account/user projection, Flagship flag evaluation.

constraints.rule: API routes use the shared auth wrappers and getDb() from @supabase/runtime; RLS identity comes from the Clerk subject.
Every flag fails closed except jobs-paused and regeneration-paused.

source.subject: feat(proxy): let signed-in users past the launch waitlist gate (DEV-190) (#889)
feat(flags): move the regeneration switch to flagship regeneration-paused (DEV-194) (#909)

nodes.label: Learning plans
nodes.role: Learning-plan domain: create/retry session boundary, attempt reservation, lifecycle service and single-transaction generation finalization, read projections, regeneration admission, task progress, status polling.

constraints.rule: Generation never runs on the HTTP request; the app reserves an attempt and hands it to the jobs Worker.

source.symbol: Generation never runs on the request

constraints.rule: Lifecycle settlement owns the single transactional finalize after generation returns.

source.subject: fix(plans): stop passing the poller as fetch's this (DEV-207) (#933)
feat(regeneration): add reasons, note and fix guidance (JCS-162) (#831)

nodes.label: AI generation
nodes.role: Generation control plane: orchestrator, provider factory/router (OpenRouter, mock), streaming parser, pacing, failure classification, timeouts, model catalog and tier model policy, cost accounting, Parallel Search client.

constraints.rule: Large single-path dependencies load inside the handler so the Worker bundle stays under the startup budget.
The jobs Worker has no tier keys, so it only reads the model catalog the app synced.

source.symbol: The jobs Worker has no tier keys

source.subject: fix(ai): keep model routes within the openrouter limit (#934)

nodes.label: Lesson content
nodes.role: Module lesson generation: preflight and claim, Worker hand-off, grounded lesson writer, code checks, verifier and repair passes, parse and commit.

constraints.rule: The module-lesson-generation Flagship flag must be on before a run is created (fail-closed).

source.subject: fix(lessons): render markdown in lesson text (#912)

nodes.label: Billing and AI budget
nodes.role: Subscription tier and Clerk Billing projection, entitlement/quota reservation, per-plan, per-user and per-tier daily AI spend ceilings, checkout return. (src/features/integrations is an empty placeholder.)

constraints.rule: Spend ceilings are enforced per plan, per user per month and per tier per day (Free, Starter and Pro each have their own daily pool).

source.subject: feat(billing): cap AI spend per user per month and globally per day (DEV-208) (#944)

nodes.label: Email notifications
nodes.role: Email notification delivery service (recipient selection, content, Resend adapter, signed unsubscribe, delivery monitor) run by the jobs Worker's email Workflow.

constraints.rule: Email delivery runs only when WORKER_ENV is production; stopping Worker email takes jobs-paused.

nodes.label: Jobs dispatch and contract
nodes.role: App-side signed HMAC client and contract for the jobs Worker plus per-job dispatchers; also holds regeneration-run, which the Worker imports to execute queued regenerations.

constraints.rule: App-to-Worker commands are HMAC-signed POST /v1/<command>; one attempt, 10 s, no automatic retry.
Start work from the app only through a signed Worker command.

source.symbol: Starting work from the app by any route other than a signed Worker command

source.subject: feat(jobs): move worker switches to flagship and drop per-job switches (DEV-193) (#899)

nodes.label: Jobs Worker
nodes.role: Cloudflare Worker (atlaris-jobs): signed HTTP commands, cron jobs, regeneration Queue consumer and the plan generation, module lessons and email delivery Workflows. Thin entry layer over src/features logic.

constraints.rule: Never create a module-level pool; open the database through withInvocationDb or withStepDb.
Never import next, @clerk/*, @vercel/* or react on a job path.
Every job stops while the Flagship flag jobs-paused is on (fails open).

source.subject: fix(workers): lazy-load the openrouter sdk to cut worker startup cpu (#754)

nodes.label: Database layer
nodes.role: Drizzle schema, migrations, RLS policies and DB clients (request-scoped RLS, service-role) in supabase/, plus query helpers in src/lib/db/queries. '@supabase/*' is a repo path alias, not an npm package.

constraints.rule: Request handlers use getDb() inside auth wrappers; tests, workers and migrations use the service-role client only where appropriate.
@supabase/* resolves to ./supabase/*, not an npm package.

source.subject: ci(db): apply production expand migrations on push to main (DEV-191) (#888)

nodes.label: Shared core
nodes.role: Foundation used by every module: shared types/constants/schemas, typed env access, logger, Sentry and PostHog wiring, utilities. Sentry/PostHog are wired here and are not separate nodes (20-node cap).

constraints.rule: Shared types are imported from src/shared/types; the README tree calls this directory types/.

nodes.label: Supabase Postgres
nodes.role: Hosted Supabase Postgres (staging atlaris-dev, production atlaris-prod). App connects with postgres-js via RLS or service-role clients; the Worker connects through Cloudflare Hyperdrive. Tables include learning_plans, generation_attempts, modules, tasks, job_queue, users, usage_metrics.

constraints.rule: RLS policies are scoped to the authenticated role; ownership resolves through users.id from the auth subject.

nodes.label: Clerk
nodes.role: Identity (sign-in, sessions, middleware), Clerk Billing (subscriptions, checkout) and user/billing webhooks.

constraints.rule: The launch waitlist gate relies on Clerk sign-up mode being Waitlist.

nodes.label: OpenRouter
nodes.role: LLM gateway for plan outlines, lessons and verifiers; the Worker reaches it through a Cloudflare AI Gateway URL; per-tier guardrails list allowed models.

constraints.rule: Model route lists stay within OPENROUTER_MAX_ROUTE_MODELS.

nodes.label: Parallel Search
nodes.role: Web search API called directly for grounded plan research (flag parallel-direct-research).

constraints.rule: Direct research runs only while the parallel-direct-research Flagship flag is on.

nodes.label: Resend
nodes.role: Transactional email provider for notification digests (sender mail.atlaris.app).

constraints.rule: The sender domain must be verified in Resend.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Queue (regeneration)
nodes.role: atlaris-regeneration-<mode> queue (maxBatchSize 1, maxRetries 3, no dead-letter queue). job_queue in Postgres stays the record; a 15-minute sweep re-sends lost work.

constraints.rule: No dead-letter queue; job_queue is the record and the sweep re-sends lost work.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Workflows
nodes.role: Durable Workflow instances: plan generation (one per reserved attempt), module lessons, and email delivery (scheduled daily 14:00 UTC and weekly MON 14:30 UTC when deployed).

constraints.rule: Workflow step names are final once deployed: never rename, reorder or remove while instances may be in flight.

source.symbol: Step names are final once deployed

nodes.label: Cloudflare Flagship
nodes.role: Feature-flag and job-switch service: launch-waitlist, maintenance-mode, grounded-generation, module-lesson-generation, jobs-paused, regeneration-paused and others. App reads over HTTP via OpenFeature; Worker via the FLAGS binding.

constraints.rule: Flags are created only in the Flagship dashboard, never from code.

source.symbol: Flags are created only in the Flagship dashboard

edges.note: Client hooks that live in features/plans create/retry and poll status
Per-request RLS client keyed to the Clerk subject
Site gate reads launch-waitlist and maintenance-mode
Plan row, attempt reservation, single-transaction finalize
After finalize, first modules get lessons
Usage cost vs plan AI ceiling
Regeneration run reuses model resolution and usage summing
Worker imports the app regeneration-run logic
Reuses service-role db inside a per-invocation pool
Pool over Hyperdrive, closed per invocation or step

flows.name: Create a learning plan
flows.trigger: User submits the create-plan form on /plans/new (POST /api/v1/plans).

steps.action: startCreate: create plan, reserve attempt slot
Finalize: attempt + modules/tasks + plan status + usage in one transaction
GET /api/v1/plans/:planId/status polled by the plan page

flows.outcome: Plan row and a reserved attempt exist; the jobs Worker's Workflow generates, finalizes plan + modules/tasks + usage in one transaction, and the plan page polling /status sees ready or failed.

flows.name: Generate module lessons
flows.trigger: User opens a module page and starts lesson generation (POST .../lesson-content/generate), or finalize enqueues the first modules.
flows.outcome: Module lessons are generated by the lessons Workflow, checked, committed to the DB, and the module page polling /lesson-content/status shows them.

flows.name: Regenerate a plan (queued)
flows.trigger: User confirms Regenerate on a plan (POST /api/v1/plans/:planId/regenerate).

steps.action: POST regenerate route: model + spend checks
Provider run for the regenerated outline

flows.outcome: job_queue row is the record; the Worker publishes it to the Cloudflare Queue, the consumer runs the regeneration and finalizes; a 15-minute sweep re-sends any pending row.

flows.name: Subscription change reaches the app
flows.trigger: Clerk emits a Billing/user webhook (subscription created, updated, canceled; user deleted).

steps.action: POST /api/v1/clerk/billing/webhook: IP rate limit, body cap, verify
Backend subscription read for the user

flows.outcome: users.subscriptionTier (and status) is projected locally, so the next request resolves the new tier for limits, models and spend ceilings. Operators can re-run via /api/internal/maintenance/billing/reconcile-clerk.

flows.name: Email notification delivery
flows.trigger: Cloudflare Workflow schedules (daily 14:00 UTC, weekly MON 14:30 UTC in deployed modes), or an operator POST to /api/internal/maintenance/notifications/email.

steps.action: Select recipients, claim and record deliveries

flows.outcome: Opted-in users get daily/weekly digests via Resend; delivery runs and per-recipient deliveries are recorded in Postgres.

mismatches.why: Two different things share 'plan': a learning plan (src/features/plans, learning_plans) and a subscription tier. UI copy says 'Free plan' for the tier and also for the single learning plan a Free account keeps (FreeAccessPlanSelector); billing even holds plan-ai-budget.ts, which is per learning plan.

our_word_sources.symbol: Free plans always use the OpenRouter free router

mismatches.code_name: src/features/jobs (app dispatch + regeneration-run) vs workers/jobs (the Worker) vs job_queue (table)
mismatches.why: 'jobs' names three places. src/features/jobs is not the Worker: it holds the app's dispatchers and regeneration-run, which the Worker imports; workers/jobs is the Worker; job_queue is the DB record for regeneration. Editing 'the jobs code' in the wrong one changes the wrong runtime.

'The queue' is two stores. job_queue in Postgres is the record; the Cloudflare Queue only carries { v, jobId } messages and has no dead-letter queue. Fixing 'queue' bugs in the wrong one loses or duplicates work.

These are operator routes inside the Next.js app, not the Cloudflare jobs Worker. File and env names say 'worker' (internal-worker-access.ts, MAINTENANCE_WORKER_TOKEN), so 'worker' is ambiguous. Renaming the env var is a deploy change, so rename the phrase in docs to 'maintenance routes'.
Same feature, three names: the directory and API route say lesson-content, the Workflow and Flagship flag say module lessons, the UI says lessons. A grep for one misses the others.
@supabase/runtime, @supabase/rls, @supabase/schema are local files (Drizzle + postgres-js), not the Supabase npm SDK, and the DB layer is split across supabase/ and src/lib/db.
UI copy calls a learning plan its 'roadmap' (Review roadmap, View roadmap, RoadmapPreview); the code never does, so searching 'roadmap' finds only presentation files.
Next 16 calls it the proxy and AGENTS.md says 'Proxy, site gate, flags', but docs still say Clerk middleware and one policy file is still named middleware-policy.ts.

src/features/plans/workflows and src/features/notifications/email/workflows hold only shared type files; the Workflow logic lives under workers/jobs/src/workflows. A folder named workflows in src suggests logic that is not there.
README's project tree lists src/types and src/lib/integrations; neither exists. Shared types live in src/shared/types, and integrations is an empty placeholder under src/features.
Docs and config comments say AI Gateway; the secret names say OPENROUTER_BASE_URL (which holds the gateway's /openrouter URL).

our_word_sources.symbol: Cloudflare AI Gateway in front of OpenRouter
